{{BLP sources|date=February 2017}}

'''Ayyalusamy Ramamoorthy''' is a professor at [[Florida State University]], where he also serves as a scientist with the [[National High Magnetic Field Laboratory]]. In 2018, he was elected as a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 November 2018|title=Two elected Fellows of Royal Society of Chemistry|url=https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/news-events/all-news/search-news/two-elected-fellows-of-royal-society-of-chemistry.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919031330/https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/news-events/all-news/search-news/two-elected-fellows-of-royal-society-of-chemistry.html |archive-date=2020-09-19 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
He received a Ph.D. in chemistry from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] in 1990. He is graduated in Chemistry of 1984 batch from [[V.O.C. Arts & Science College]], [[Tuticorin]], [[Tamil Nadu]].{{Citation needed|date= August 2025}}

==Career==
His main area of research is the development of solid-state [[NMR]] and its applications to non-soluble, non-crystalline chemical and biological solids.<ref>[http://www.ns.umich.edu/htdocs/releases/story.php?id=3190 Natural antibiotics yield secrets to atom-level imaging technique], NewsService, [[University of Michigan]]</ref><ref>[http://ase.tufts.edu/chemistry/kumar/group/html/8537sci2.html Fluorous Peptides Get Ready To Heal], </ref> He is known for the development of solid-state NMR methods (such as USEME, PISEMA, PITANSEMA, HIMSELF, etc.)<ref name="urlSolid-State NMR Reveals Key Structural Features of Membrane Transport Proteins">{{cite journal  |doi=10.1063/1.1325226 |bibcode=2000PhT....53i..19D |title=Solid-State NMR Reveals Key Structural Features of Membrane Transport Proteins |journal= Physics Today|year=2000 |last1=Day |first1=Charles |volume=53 |issue=9 |pages=19–22 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and as a researcher of membrane-associated peptides and proteins, an organizer of international symposia, and author of a book on [[NMR Spectroscopy]] of biological [[solid]]s.<ref>[http://www.internetchemie.info/news/2007/sep07/blowtorch.html Revealing the workings of 'Mother Nature's blowtorch'], by Internetchemistry.com</ref><ref>[http://www.ns.umich.edu/htdocs/releases/story.php?id=6522 New insights into cause of diabetes emerge from U-M research] NewsService, [[University of Michigan]]</ref> He was also involved in the characterization of new [[nanomaterial]]s.<ref>[https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2007/10/071004143114.htm New Plastic Is Strong As Steel, Transparent], [[ScienceDaily]]</ref> He teaches Chemistry, Biophysics and NMR to undergraduate and graduate students at the University of Michigan.
